questions.q: Consider a circle with its centre lying on the focus of the parabola \(y^2=2px\) such that it touches the directrix of the parabola. Then a point of intersection of the circle and parabola is
questions.sol: Circle: \(\left(x-\dfrac p2\right)^2+y^2=p^2\). With \(y^2=2px\): \(x^2+px-\dfrac{3p^2}4=0\), so \(x=\dfrac p2\) (the other root is negative), \(y=\pm p\).

questions.q: If \(x+y=k\) is normal to \(y^2=12x\), then \(k\) is
questions.sol: Normal of slope \(m\): \(y=mx-2am-am^3\) with \(a=3\), \(m=-1\): \(y=-x+9\).

questions.q: If the line \(x-1=0\) is the directrix of the parabola \(y^2-kx+8=0\), then one of the values of \(k\) is
questions.sol: \(y^2=k\left(x-\dfrac8k\right)\): directrix \(x=\dfrac8k-\dfrac k4=1\) gives \(k^2+4k-32=0\), \(k=4\) or \(-8\).

questions.q: The equation of the directrix of the parabola \(y^2+4y+4x+2=0\) is
questions.sol: \((y+2)^2=-4\left(x-\dfrac12\right)\): opens to the left with \(a=1\), directrix \(x=\dfrac12+1\).

questions.q: The equation of the common tangent touching the circle \((x-3)^2+y^2=9\) and the parabola \(y^2=4x\) above the \(x\)-axis is
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac1m\) is at distance \(3\) from \((3,0)\): \(\left(3m+\dfrac1m\right)^2=9(1+m^2)\) gives \(m^2=\dfrac13\); above the axis \(m=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: The locus of the mid point of the line segment joining the focus to a moving point on the parabola \(y^2=4ax\) is another parabola with directrix
questions.sol: Mid point \(h=\dfrac{a+at^2}2\), \(k=at\): \(k^2=2a\left(h-\dfrac a2\right)\) — vertex \(\left(\dfrac a2,0\right)\), focal distance \(\dfrac a2\), directrix \(x=0\).

questions.q: The equation of the common tangent to the curves \(y^2=8x\) and \(xy=-1\) is
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac2m\) in \(xy=-1\): \(mx^2+\dfrac{2x}m+1=0\) has equal roots when \(m^3=1\).

questions.q: The focal chord to \(y^2=16x\) is tangent to \((x-6)^2+y^2=2\), then the possible values of the slope of this chord, are
questions.sol: Chord \(y=m(x-4)\) at distance \(\sqrt2\) from \((6,0)\): \(4m^2=2(1+m^2)\).

questions.q: The angle between the tangents drawn from the point \((1,4)\) to the parabola \(y^2=4x\) is
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac1m\) through \((1,4)\): \(m^2-4m+1=0\). \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{|m_1-m_2|}{1+m_1m_2}=\dfrac{\sqrt{12}}2=\sqrt3\).

questions.q: The axis of a parabola is along the line \(y=x\) and the distances of its vertex and focus from origin are \(\sqrt2\) and \(2\sqrt2\) respectively. If vertex and focus both lie in the first quadrant, then the equation of the parabola is

Consider the two curves
\(C_1:y^2=4x\)
\(C_2:x^2+y^2-6x+1=0\). Then,
opts: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) touch each other only at one point
\(C_1\) and \(C_2\) touch each other exactly at two points
\(C_1\) and \(C_2\) intersect (but do not touch) at exactly two points
\(C_1\) and \(C_2\) neither intersect nor touch each other.
questions.sol: Eliminating \(y\): \(x^2-2x+1=0\), a double root \(x=1\), with \(y=\pm2\).

questions.q: Let \((x,y)\) be any point on the parabola \(y^2=4x\). Let \(P\) be the point that divides the line segment from \((0,0)\) to \((x,y)\) in the ratio \(1:3\). Then the locus of \(P\) is
questions.sol: \(P(h,k)=\left(\dfrac x4,\dfrac y4\right)\): \((4k)^2=4(4h)\).

questions.q: The common tangents to the circle \(x^2+y^2=2\) and the parabola \(y^2=8x\) touch the circle at the point \(P,Q\) and the parabola at the points \(R,S\). Then the area of the quadrilateral \(PQRS\) is
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac2m\) touches the circle when \(\dfrac4{m^2}=2(1+m^2)\): \(m=\pm1\). Contact points \((-1,\pm1)\) and \((2,\pm4)\): a trapezium with parallel sides \(2\), \(8\) and height \(3\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a point on the parabola \(y^2=4ax\), where \(a>0\). The normal to the parabola at \(P\) meets the \(x\)-axis at a point \(Q\). The area of the triangle \(PFQ\), where \(F\) is the focus of the parabola, is \(120\). If the slope \(m\) of the normal and \(a\) are both positive integers, then the pair \((a,m)\) is
The equations of the common tangents to the parabola \(y=x^2\) and \(y=-(x-2)^2\) is/are
questions.sol: Tangent to \(y=x^2\) at \((t,t^2)\): \(y=2tx-t^2\). In the second curve: \(x^2+(2t-4)x+4-t^2=0\) has equal roots when \(8t^2-16t=0\): \(t=0,2\).

questions.q: The tangent \(PT\) and the normal \(PN\) to the parabola \(y^2=4ax\) at a point \(P\) on it meet its axis at points \(T\) and \(N\), respectively. The locus of the centroid of the triangle \(PTN\) is a parabola whose
questions.sol: \(T(-at^2,0)\), \(N(2a+at^2,0)\): centroid \(h=\dfrac{2a+at^2}3\), \(k=\dfrac{2at}3\), so \(k^2=\dfrac{4a}3\left(h-\dfrac{2a}3\right)\). Vertex \(\left(\dfrac{2a}3,0\right)\), latus rectum \(\dfrac{4a}3\), focus \(\left(\dfrac{2a}3+\dfrac a3,0\right)\), directrix \(x=\dfrac a3\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be two distinct points on the parabola \(y^2=4x\). If the axis of the parabola touches a circle of radius \(r\) having \(AB\) as its diameter, then the slope of the line joining \(A\) and \(B\) can be
questions.sol: For \(A(t_1^2,2t_1)\), \(B(t_2^2,2t_2)\) the centre has ordinate \(t_1+t_2=\pm r\), and the slope of \(AB\) is \(\dfrac2{t_1+t_2}\).

questions.q: Let \(L\) be a normal to the parabola \(y^2=4x\). If \(L\) passes through the point \((9,6)\), then \(L\) is given by

Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be distinct points on the parabola \(y^2=2x\) such that a circle with \(PQ\) as diameter passes through the vertex \(O\) of the parabola. If \(P\) lies in the first quadrant and the area of the triangle \(OPQ\) is \(3\sqrt2\), then which of the following is (are) the coordinates of \(P\)?
questions.sol: \(P\left(\dfrac{t_1^2}2,t_1\right)\), \(Q\left(\dfrac{t_2^2}2,t_2\right)\); \(OP\perp OQ\) gives \(t_1t_2=-4\). Area \(=\dfrac14|t_1t_2||t_1-t_2|=t_1+\dfrac4{t_1}=3\sqrt2\), so \(t_1=2\sqrt2\) or \(\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The circle \(C_1:x^2+y^2=3\), with centre at \(O\), intersects the parabola \(x^2=2y\) at the point \(P\) in the first quadrant. Let the tangent to the circle \(C_1\) at \(P\) touches other two circles \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) at \(R_2\) and \(R_3\), respectively. Suppose \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) have equal radii \(2\sqrt3\) and centres \(Q_2\) and \(Q_3\), respectively. If \(Q_2\) and \(Q_3\) lie on the \(y\)-axis, then
questions.sol: \(P=(\sqrt2,1)\), tangent \(\sqrt2x+y=3\). Centre \((0,c)\): \(\dfrac{|c-3|}{\sqrt3}=2\sqrt3\), \(c=9,-3\): \(Q_2Q_3=12\). \(R_2R_3=\sqrt{12^2-(4\sqrt3)^2}=4\sqrt6\). Area \(OR_2R_3=\dfrac12\cdot4\sqrt6\cdot\sqrt3=6\sqrt2\). Area \(PQ_2Q_3=\dfrac12\cdot12\cdot\sqrt2=6\sqrt2\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be the point on the parabola \(y^2=4x\) which is at the shortest distance from the centre \(S\) of the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x-16y+64=0\). Let \(Q\) be the point on the circle dividing the line segment \(SP\) internally. Then
opts: the \(x\)-intercept of the normal to the parabola at \(P\) is \(6\)
the slope of the tangent to the circle at \(Q\) is \(\dfrac12\)
questions.sol: \(S=(2,8)\), radius \(2\). The normal \(y=mx-2m-m^3\) through \(S\): \(m^3=-8\), \(m=-2\), \(P=(4,4)\). \(SP=2\sqrt5\); \(SQ:QP=2:(2\sqrt5-2)=(\sqrt5+1):4\); normal \(y-4=-2(x-4)\) meets the axis at \(x=6\); tangent at \(Q\) is perpendicular to \(SP\): slope \(\dfrac12\).

questions.q: If a chord, which is not a tangent, of the parabola \(y^2=16x\) has the equation \(2x+y=p\), and midpoint \((h,k)\), then which of the following is (are) possible value(s) of \(p\), \(h\) and \(k\)?
questions.sol: Chord with mid point \((h,k)\): \(ky-8(x+h)=k^2-16h\), i.e. \(8x-ky=8h-k^2\). Comparing with \(2x+y=p\): \(k=-4\) and \(p=2h-4\).

questions.q: Let \(E\) denote the parabola \(y^2=8x\). Let \(P=(-2,4)\), and let \(Q\) and \(Q'\) be two distinct points on \(E\) such that the lines \(PQ\) and \(PQ'\) are tangents to \(E\). Let \(F\) be the focus of \(E\). Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
opts: The triangle \(PFQ\) is a right-angled triangle
The triangle \(QPQ'\) is a right-angled triangle
\(F\) lies on the line joining \(Q\) and \(Q'\)
questions.sol: \(P\) lies on the directrix \(x=-2\). Tangents from a point of the directrix are perpendicular, their chord of contact is a focal chord, and \(PF\) is perpendicular to it. \(PF=\sqrt{16+16}=4\sqrt2\).

questions.q: Consider the parabola \(y^2=4x\). Let \(S\) be the focus of the parabola. A pair of tangents drawn to the parabola from the point \(P=(-2,1)\) meet the parabola at \(P_1\) and \(P_2\). Let \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) be the points on the lines \(SP_1\) and \(SP_2\) respectively such that \(PQ_1\) is perpendicular to \(SP_1\) and \(PQ_2\) is perpendicular to \(SP_2\). Then, which of the following is/are true?

Let \(A_1,B_1,C_1\) be three points in the \(xy\)-plane. Suppose that the lines \(A_1C_1\) and \(B_1C_1\) are tangents to the curve \(y^2=8x\) at \(A_1\) and \(B_1\), respectively. If \(O=(0,0)\) and \(C_1=(-4,0)\), then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
opts: The length of the line segment \(OA_1\) is \(4\sqrt3\)
The length of the line segment \(A_1B_1\) is \(16\)
The orthocenter of the triangle \(A_1B_1C_1\) is \((0,0)\)
The orthocenter of the triangle \(A_1B_1C_1\) is \((1,0)\)
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac2m\) through \((-4,0)\): \(m^2=\dfrac12\); contact points \(\left(\dfrac2{m^2},\dfrac4m\right)=(4,\pm4\sqrt2)\). \(OA_1=\sqrt{48}\), \(A_1B_1=8\sqrt2\). Altitude from \(A_1\) (perpendicular to \(B_1C_1\), slope \(-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\)): \(y-4\sqrt2=\sqrt2(x-4)\) meets the \(x\)-axis (altitude from \(C_1\)) at the origin.

questions.q: Suppose that the normals drawn at three different points on the parabola \(y^2=4x\) pass through the point \((h,0)\). Show that \(h>2\).
questions.sol: The normal \(y=mx-2m-m^3\) passes through \((h,0)\) when \(m(m^2+2-h)=0\). Three different normals need \(m^2=h-2>0\).

questions.q: \(A\) is a point on the parabola \(y^2=4ax\). The normal at \(A\) cuts the parabola again at \(B\). If \(AB\) subtends a right angle at the vertex of the parabola, find the slope of \(AB\).
questions.sol: \(t_2=-t_1-\dfrac2{t_1}\) and the right angle at the vertex gives \(t_1t_2=-4\): \(t_1^2=2\). Slope of \(AB=\dfrac2{t_1+t_2}=-t_1\).

questions.q: Find the equation of the normal to the curve \(x^2=4y\) which passes through the point \((1,2)\).

Three normals are drawn from the point \((c,0)\) to the curve \(y^2=x\). Show that \(c\) must be greater than \(\dfrac12\). One normal is always the \(x\)-axis. Find \(c\) for which the other two normals are perpendicular to each other.
questions.sol: With \(a=\dfrac14\) the normal is \(y=mx-\dfrac m2-\dfrac{m^3}4\); through \((c,0)\): \(m=0\) or \(m^2=4c-2\), real and non-zero when \(c>\dfrac12\). Perpendicular: \(-(4c-2)=-1\).

questions.q: Through the vertex '\(O\)' of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) chords \(OP\) and \(OQ\) are drawn at right angles, show that for all positions of \(P\), \(PQ\) cuts the axis of the parabola at a fixed point. Also find the locus of the mid point of \(PQ\).
Show that the locus of a point that divides a chord of slope \(2\) of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) internally in the ratio \(1:2\) is parabola. Find its vertex.

Points \(A,B,C\) lie on the parabola \(y^2=4ax\). The tangent to the parabola at \(A,B\) and \(C\) taken in pair intersect at the points \(P,Q\) and \(R\). Determine the ratio of the areas of the \(\Delta ABC\) and \(\Delta PQR\).
questions.sol: With parameters \(t_1,t_2,t_3\): area \(ABC=a^2|(t_1-t_2)(t_2-t_3)(t_3-t_1)|\). The tangents meet at \((at_1t_2,a(t_1+t_2))\) etc., and the area of \(PQR\) comes to \(\dfrac{a^2}2|(t_1-t_2)(t_2-t_3)(t_3-t_1)|\).

questions.q: From a point \(A\) common tangents are drawn to the circle \(x^2+y^2=\dfrac{a^2}2\) and the parabola \(y^2=4ax\). Then find the area of the quadrilateral formed by the common tangents drawn from \(A\) and the chord of contact of the circle and the parabola.
questions.sol: \(y=mx+\dfrac am\) touches the circle when \(m^4+m^2-2=0\): \(m=\pm1\), \(A=(-a,0)\). Chords of contact: \(x=-\dfrac a2\) (points \(\left(-\dfrac a2,\pm\dfrac a2\right)\)) and \(x=a\) (points \((a,\pm2a)\)). Trapezium: \(\dfrac12(a+4a)\cdot\dfrac{3a}2\).

questions.q: Let \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be, respectively, the parabolas \(x^2=y-1\) and \(y^2=x-1\), let \(P\) be any point on \(C_1\) and \(Q\) be any point on \(C_2\). Let \(P_1\) and \(Q_1\) be the reflections of \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively, with respect to the line \(y=x\). Prove that \(P_1\) lies on \(C_2\), \(Q_1\) lies on \(C_1\) and \(PQ\ge\min[PP_1,QQ_1]\). Hence or otherwise determine points \(P_0\) and \(Q_0\) on the parabolas \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) respectively such that \(P_0Q_0\le PQ\) for all pairs of points \((P,Q)\) with \(P\) on \(C_1\) and \(Q\) on \(C_2\).
questions.sol: Interchanging \(x\) and \(y\) turns \(C_1\) into \(C_2\), so \(P_1\in C_2\), \(Q_1\in C_1\). \(C_1\) lies above \(y=x\) and \(C_2\) below it, so \(PQ\ge\) (distance of \(P\) from the line) + (distance of \(Q\) from the line) \(=\dfrac{PP_1+QQ_1}2\ge\min[PP_1,QQ_1]\). The distance of \((t,t^2+1)\) from \(y=x\) is \(\dfrac{t^2-t+1}{\sqrt2}\), least at \(t=\dfrac12\): \(P_0=\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac54\right)\) and \(Q_0\) is its reflection.

questions.q: Three normals with slopes \(m_1,m_2\) and \(m_3\) are drawn from a point \(P\) not on the axis of the parabola \(y^2=4x\). If \(m_1m_2=\alpha\), results in the locus of \(P\) being a part of the parabola, find the value of \(\alpha\).
questions.sol: For \(P(h,k)\): \(m^3+(2-h)m+k=0\), \(m_1m_2m_3=-k\), so \(m_3=-\dfrac k\alpha\). Substituting: \(k^2=\alpha^2h+\alpha^3-2\alpha^2\). This is part of \(y^2=4x\) when \(\alpha^2=4\) and \(\alpha^3=2\alpha^2\).

questions.q: At any point \(P\) on the parabola \(y^2-2y-4x+5=0\), a tangent is drawn which meets the directrix at \(Q\). Find the locus of point \(R\) which divides \(QP\) externally in the ratio \(\dfrac12:1\).
questions.sol: \((y-1)^2=4(x-1)\): \(P=(1+t^2,1+2t)\), tangent \(t(y-1)=(x-1)+t^2\) meets the directrix \(x=0\) at \(Q=\left(0,1+t-\dfrac1t\right)\). \(R=2Q-P=\left(-1-t^2,1-\dfrac2t\right)\); eliminate \(t\).

questions.q:
Match the following :
Normals are drawn at points \(P,Q\) and \(R\) lying on the parabola \(y^2=4x\) which intersect at \((3,0)\). Then
Column 1Column 2
(i) Area of \(\Delta PQR\)(A) \(2\)
(ii) Radius of circumcircle of \(\Delta PQR\)(B) \(5/2\)
(iii) Centroid of \(\Delta PQR\)(C) \((5/2,0)\)
(iv) Circumcentre of \(\Delta PQR\)(D) \((2/3,0)\)
questions.sol: \(m^3-m=0\): \(m=0,\pm1\), feet \((m^2,-2m)\): \((0,0)\), \((1,-2)\), \((1,2)\). Area \(=\dfrac12\cdot4\cdot1\); centroid \(\left(\dfrac23,0\right)\); circumcentre \((h,0)\) with \(h^2=(1-h)^2+4\): \(h=\dfrac52\), which is also the radius.

If \(P\) is a point on \(C_1\) and \(Q\) is another point on \(C_2\), then \(\dfrac{PA^2+PB^2+PC^2+PD^2}{QA^2+QB^2+QC^2+QD^2}\) is equal to

Let \(ABCD\) be a square of side length \(2\) units. \(C_2\) is the circle through vertices \(A,B,C,D\) and \(C_1\) is the circle touching all the sides of the square \(ABCD\). \(L\) is a line through \(A\).
A circle touches the line \(L\) and the circle \(C_1\) externally such that both the circles are on the same side of the line, then the locus of centre of the circle is
questions.sol: If the radius is \(\rho\), the centre is at distance \(\rho+1\) from the centre of \(C_1\) and \(\rho\) from \(L\), i.e. \(\rho+1\) from a line parallel to \(L\): focus–directrix property of a parabola.

Let \(ABCD\) be a square of side length \(2\) units. \(C_2\) is the circle through vertices \(A,B,C,D\) and \(C_1\) is the circle touching all the sides of the square \(ABCD\). \(L\) is a line through \(A\).
A line \(M\) through \(A\) is drawn parallel to \(BD\). Point \(S\) moves such that its distances from the line \(BD\) and the vertex \(A\) are equal. If locus of \(S\) cuts \(M\) at \(T_2\) and \(T_3\) and \(AC\) at \(T_1\), then area of \(\Delta T_1T_2T_3\) is
questions.sol: The locus is a parabola with focus \(A\) and directrix \(BD\): distance \(\sqrt2=2a\). \(T_2T_3\) is the latus rectum \(4a=2\sqrt2\) and \(T_1\) the vertex, at distance \(a=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\) from it. Area \(=\dfrac12\cdot2\sqrt2\cdot\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\).

Consider the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) and the parabola \(y^2=8x\). They intersect at \(P\) and \(Q\) in the first and the fourth quadrants, respectively. Tangents to the circle at \(P\) and \(Q\) intersect the \(x\)-axis at \(R\) and tangents to the parabola at \(P\) and \(Q\) intersect the \(x\)-axis at \(S\).
The ratio of the areas of the triangles \(PQS\) and \(PQR\) is
questions.sol: \(x^2+8x-9=0\) gives \(x=1\): \(P=(1,2\sqrt2)\), \(Q=(1,-2\sqrt2)\). Tangent to the circle at \(P\): \(x+2\sqrt2y=9\), so \(R=(9,0)\); tangent to the parabola: \(2\sqrt2y=4(x+1)\), so \(S=(-1,0)\). Both triangles have base \(PQ\) (on \(x=1\)); heights \(2\) and \(8\).

questions.q:

Consider the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) and the parabola \(y^2=8x\). They intersect at \(P\) and \(Q\) in the first and the fourth quadrants, respectively. Tangents to the circle at \(P\) and \(Q\) intersect the \(x\)-axis at \(R\) and tangents to the parabola at \(P\) and \(Q\) intersect the \(x\)-axis at \(S\).
The radius of the circumcircle of the triangle \(PRS\) is
questions.sol: \(x^2+8x-9=0\) gives \(x=1\): \(P=(1,2\sqrt2)\), \(Q=(1,-2\sqrt2)\). Tangent to the circle at \(P\): \(x+2\sqrt2y=9\), so \(R=(9,0)\); tangent to the parabola: \(2\sqrt2y=4(x+1)\), so \(S=(-1,0)\). \(RS=10\), \(PS=2\sqrt3\), \(PR=6\sqrt2\), area \(=\dfrac12\cdot10\cdot2\sqrt2\). \(R=\dfrac{abc}{4\Delta}=\dfrac{10\cdot2\sqrt3\cdot6\sqrt2}{40\sqrt2}\).

Consider the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) and the parabola \(y^2=8x\). They intersect at \(P\) and \(Q\) in the first and the fourth quadrants, respectively. Tangents to the circle at \(P\) and \(Q\) intersect the \(x\)-axis at \(R\) and tangents to the parabola at \(P\) and \(Q\) intersect the \(x\)-axis at \(S\).
The radius of the incircle of the triangle \(PQR\) is
questions.sol: \(x^2+8x-9=0\) gives \(x=1\): \(P=(1,2\sqrt2)\), \(Q=(1,-2\sqrt2)\). Tangent to the circle at \(P\): \(x+2\sqrt2y=9\), so \(R=(9,0)\); tangent to the parabola: \(2\sqrt2y=4(x+1)\), so \(S=(-1,0)\). \(PQ=4\sqrt2\), \(PR=QR=6\sqrt2\): \(s=8\sqrt2\), area \(=\dfrac12\cdot4\sqrt2\cdot8=16\sqrt2\), \(r=\dfrac\Delta s\).

Let \(PQ\) be a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=4ax\). The tangents to the parabola at \(P\) and \(Q\) meet at a point lying on the line \(y=2x+a\), \(a>0\).
Length of the chord \(PQ\) is
questions.sol: Tangents at the ends of a focal chord meet on the directrix: the point is \((-a,-a)\), so \(t_1t_2=-1\) and \(t_1+t_2=-1\). Focal chord length \(=a(t_1-t_2)^2=a\left[(t_1+t_2)^2-4t_1t_2\right]\).

Let \(PQ\) be a focal chord of the parabola \(y^2=4ax\). The tangents to the parabola at \(P\) and \(Q\) meet at a point lying on the line \(y=2x+a\), \(a>0\).
If chord \(PQ\) subtends an angle \(\theta\) at the vertex of \(y^2=4ax\), then \(\tan\theta=\)
questions.sol: Tangents at the ends of a focal chord meet on the directrix: the point is \((-a,-a)\), so \(t_1t_2=-1\) and \(t_1+t_2=-1\). Slopes of \(OP,OQ\) are \(\dfrac2{t_1},\dfrac2{t_2}\): \(|\tan\theta|=\dfrac{2|t_1-t_2|}{|t_1t_2+4|}=\dfrac{2\sqrt5}3\). Since \(\vec{OP}\cdot\vec{OQ}=a^2(t_1^2t_2^2+4t_1t_2)<0\), the angle is obtuse.

Let \(a,r,s,t\) be non-zero real numbers. Let \(P(at^2,2at)\), \(Q\), \(R(ar^2,2ar)\) and \(S(as^2,2as)\) be distinct points on the parabola \(y^2=4ax\). Suppose that \(PQ\) is the focal chord and lines \(QR\) and \(PK\) are parallel, where \(K\) is the point \((2a,0)\).
The value of \(r\) is
questions.sol: \(Q\) has parameter \(-\dfrac1t\). Slope of \(QR=\dfrac2{r-\frac1t}\), slope of \(PK=\dfrac{2at}{at^2-2a}=\dfrac{2t}{t^2-2}\). Equating: \(r-\dfrac1t=\dfrac{t^2-2}t\).

Let \(a,r,s,t\) be non-zero real numbers. Let \(P(at^2,2at)\), \(Q\), \(R(ar^2,2ar)\) and \(S(as^2,2as)\) be distinct points on the parabola \(y^2=4ax\). Suppose that \(PQ\) is the focal chord and lines \(QR\) and \(PK\) are parallel, where \(K\) is the point \((2a,0)\).
If \(st=1\), then the tangent at \(P\) and the normal at \(S\) to the parabola meet at a point whose ordinate is
questions.sol: Tangent at \(P\): \(x=ty-at^2\). Normal at \(S\) \(\left(s=\dfrac1t\right)\): \(y=-\dfrac xt+\dfrac{2a}t+\dfrac a{t^3}\). Substituting: \(2y=at+\dfrac{2a}t+\dfrac a{t^3}=\dfrac{a(t^2+1)^2}{t^3}\).

questions.sol: \(y=-\dfrac12(x-1)^2+\dfrac32\) is a parabola with axis \(x=1\).

questions.q: Consider the parabola \(y^2=8x\). Let \(\Delta_1\) be the area of the triangle formed by the end points of its latus rectum and the point \(P\left(\dfrac12,2\right)\) on the parabola, and \(\Delta_2\) be the area of the triangle formed by drawing tangents at \(P\) and at the end points of the latus rectum. Then \(\dfrac{\Delta_1}{\Delta_2}\) is
questions.sol: For any three points of a parabola, the triangle of the points has twice the area of the triangle formed by the tangents at them.

Let the curve \(C\) be the mirror image of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) with respect to the line \(x+y+4=0\). If \(A\) and \(B\) are the points of intersection of \(C\) with the line \(y=-5\), then the distance between \(A\) and \(B\) is
questions.sol: Reflection in \(x+y+4=0\) sends \((x,y)\) to \((-y-4,-x-4)\), so the line \(y=-5\) is the image of \(x=1\), which meets \(y^2=4x\) at \((1,\pm2)\) — the latus rectum, of length \(4\). Reflection preserves lengths.

questions.q: If the normals of the parabola \(y^2=4x\) drawn at the end points of its latus rectum are tangents to the circle \((x-3)^2+(y+2)^2=r^2\), then the value of \(r^2\) is
questions.sol: Normals at \((1,\pm2)\): \(x+y=3\) and \(x-y=3\). Distance of \((3,-2)\) from each is \(\dfrac2{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2\).

questions.q:
Question Stem
Consider the region \(R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:x\ge0\text{ and }y^2\le4-x\}\). Let \(F\) be the family of all circles that are contained in \(R\) and have centers on the \(x\)-axis. Let \(C\) be the circle that has largest radius among the circles in \(F\). Let \((\alpha,\beta)\) be a point where the circle \(C\) meets the curve \(y^2=4-x\).
The radius of the circle \(C\) is ______.
questions.sol: The largest circle touches the \(y\)-axis (centre \((r,0)\)) and the parabola. Putting \(y^2=4-x\) in \((x-r)^2+y^2=r^2\): \(x^2-(2r+1)x+4=0\) must have equal roots: \(2r+1=4\), \(r=1.5\), and the root is \(x=2\).

questions.q:
Question Stem
Consider the region \(R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:x\ge0\text{ and }y^2\le4-x\}\). Let \(F\) be the family of all circles that are contained in \(R\) and have centers on the \(x\)-axis. Let \(C\) be the circle that has largest radius among the circles in \(F\). Let \((\alpha,\beta)\) be a point where the circle \(C\) meets the curve \(y^2=4-x\).
The value of \(\alpha\) is ______.
questions.sol: The largest circle touches the \(y\)-axis (centre \((r,0)\)) and the parabola. Putting \(y^2=4-x\) in \((x-r)^2+y^2=r^2\): \(x^2-(2r+1)x+4=0\) must have equal roots: \(2r+1=4\), \(r=1.5\), and the root is \(x=2\).

questions.q: A normal with slope \(\dfrac1{\sqrt6}\) is drawn from the point \((0,-\alpha)\) to the parabola \(x^2=-4ay\), where \(a>0\). Let \(L\) be the line passing through \((0,-\alpha)\) and parallel to the directrix of the parabola. Suppose that \(L\) intersects the parabola at two points \(A\) and \(B\). Let \(r\) denote the length of the latus rectum and \(s\) denote the square of the length of the line segment \(AB\). If \(r:s=1:16\), then the value of \(24a\) is ______.
questions.sol: On \(y=-\alpha\): \(x^2=4a\alpha\), \(s=16a\alpha\), \(r=4a\): \(\alpha=4\). At \((2at,-at^2)\) the tangent slope is \(-t\), so the normal slope \(\dfrac1t=\dfrac1{\sqrt6}\); the normal \(y+6a=\dfrac{x-2\sqrt6a}{\sqrt6}\) meets the \(y\)-axis at \(-8a=-4\): \(a=\dfrac12\).
